logs.message: POST /checkout received user_id=42
db connection acquire took 2400ms
psycopg2.OperationalError: timeout expired after 5000ms while waiting for db connection
checkout failed: db_unreachable

gold: the postgres connection pool is unable to hand out connections within 5 seconds; the checkout request fails because the database is unreachable or saturated. action: check the db pool size, the postgres server load, and any network path between the app and the database.

logs.message: GET /me started
verifying jwt iss=auth.example exp=2026-05-06T09:55:00Z
jwt validation failed: token expired
returning 401 to client

gold: the jwt presented by the client has an exp timestamp in the past, so the auth middleware rejects it and the request is returned as 401. action: ensure the client refreshes its token before expiry; verify clock sync between issuer and verifier.

logs.message: POST /search forwarded to elasticsearch
elasticsearch returned 429 retry_after=1
elasticsearch returned 429 retry_after=2
search aborted: upstream rate limit exhausted after 3 retries

gold: elasticsearch is rate-limiting the service with repeated 429 responses; after 3 retries the search request is aborted. action: lower the request rate, add jitter and exponential backoff, or request a higher rate limit from the upstream.

logs.message: loading 200k rows for analytics export
memory usage 92% rss=3.6GB
MemoryError: cannot allocate buffer
process killed by oom-killer signal=9

gold: the process tried to load 200k rows into memory which pushed rss past the container limit and the linux oom-killer terminated it. action: stream the export instead of loading it all into memory, or raise the container memory limit if streaming is impractical.

logs.message: GET /price?sku=abc -> 99.00 (cache hit)
checkout total 99.00 mismatch with current price 129.00 from db
price_inconsistency: cached_price=99.00 db_price=129.00 sku=abc

gold: the cache returned a price that is now out of date relative to the database; checkout used the stale cached value while the source of truth had moved on. action: invalidate the price cache on update and shorten ttl for price entries.

logs.message: GET /orders?user_id=42 started
slow query 8200ms: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE user_id=42 ORDER BY created_at DESC
EXPLAIN: Seq Scan on orders rows=12000000
GET /orders -> 200 8205ms

gold: the orders query is doing a sequential scan of 12 million rows because there is no usable index on user_id; this is the cause of the 8s latency. action: add an index on (user_id, created_at desc) and verify the planner uses it.

logs.message: txn-A: UPDATE accounts SET bal=bal-10 WHERE id=1
txn-B: UPDATE accounts SET bal=bal-5 WHERE id=2
txn-A: UPDATE accounts SET bal=bal+10 WHERE id=2 (waiting)
psycopg2.errors.DeadlockDetected: deadlock detected; rolling back txn-A

gold: two concurrent transactions are updating the same accounts rows in opposite order and postgres detected a deadlock; one transaction was rolled back. action: enforce a consistent lock ordering across all account-mutating transactions.

logs.message: outbound POST https://payments.partner.example/charge
ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: certificate has expired (_ssl.c:1006)
charge failed: tls verification

gold: the partner's tls certificate has expired so outbound https calls to payments.partner.example fail at handshake. action: contact the partner to rotate the cert; in the meantime no charges will succeed.

logs.message: consumer lag topic=orders partition=0 lag=42000
consumer lag topic=orders partition=0 lag=58000 (growing)
downstream sla breach: orders processing latency p99=42s

gold: the orders consumer group is falling behind on partition 0 and lag is growing, which is breaching downstream sla. action: scale out consumer instances, identify slow handlers per message, and check for poison messages causing retries.

logs.message: service starting env=staging
kafka brokers resolved to prod-kafka-1:9092 in env=staging
events flowing to prod topic from staging service: cross-environment leak detected

gold: the staging service has been pointed at the production kafka brokers and is producing real events into the prod topic. action: roll back the config change immediately; audit which events leaked and reconcile.

logs.message: redis maxmemory=2gb policy=allkeys-lru evicted_keys_total=14821
session lookup miss key=sess:abc (recently active user)
user logged out unexpectedly: session evicted from cache

gold: redis is evicting under memory pressure with maxmemory policy allkeys-lru; sessions are being dropped causing unexpected logouts. action: raise the redis maxmemory, switch to a session-only store, or move sessions to a persistent store.

logs.message: disk usage on /var/lib/postgresql=98% (47GB/48GB)
could not extend file pg_wal/0000003: No space left on device
postgres going read-only: cannot write WAL

gold: the postgres data volume is at 98% and a wal write failed with no space left on device; the database has gone read-only. action: free space on the data volume immediately (drop old WAL, truncate large tables, expand the disk).

logs.message: process fd count=8192 (limit=8192)
OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files: '/tmp/upload-9821.bin'
upload handler crashed: cannot open temp file

gold: the process has hit its open-files ulimit (8192) and cannot open a new temp file for an upload; this points to a leak where file handles are not being closed. action: audit handlers that open files for missing close() and add a ulimit alarm.

logs.message: service booting up commit=a1b2c3d
RuntimeError: missing required env var: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY
process exiting with code=1

gold: the service refused to start because STRIPE_SECRET_KEY env var is missing; the deploy template did not pass it through. action: add the secret to the deploy environment and redeploy; ensure config validation fails fast with a clear message.

logs.message: tomcat http-nio thread pool: active=200 queue_size=1024 max=200
request queued for 4200ms before dispatch
java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException: Task rejected from ThreadPoolExecutor (queue full)

gold: the tomcat http thread pool is saturated and new tasks are being rejected; downstream calls are saturating worker threads. action: investigate why upstream calls are slow, set per-call timeouts, and bound the thread pool to fail fast on overload.

logs.message: acquiring redis lock key=billing:job:nightly ttl=30s
lock still held by holder=worker-7; retrying
lock still held by holder=worker-7; retrying
billing nightly job skipped this run: lock held >90s by another worker

gold: the nightly billing redis lock is held by another worker for over 90s; this run was skipped to avoid double execution. action: investigate why the holder is slow; consider lock fencing tokens and a lower ttl.

logs.message: PutObject bucket=archive key=2026/05/06/batch.parquet size=412MB
s3 503 SlowDown: Reduce your request rate (request_id=ABCDEF)
s3 503 SlowDown: Reduce your request rate (attempt 2)
archive upload failed after 4 retries with backoff

gold: s3 is returning 503 SlowDown to the prefix being uploaded; after backoff retries the upload was abandoned. action: spread writes across more s3 prefixes (key-space partitioning) or open a support case for higher limits.

logs.message: applying migration 0042_add_currency_column.sql
migration 0042 step 3/5 failed: ERROR: cannot ALTER TABLE while concurrent index build active
schema_migrations table still pinned at 0041; database is in an inconsistent state

gold: alembic migration 0042 failed mid-run leaving the database in an inconsistent state where schema_migrations still records 0041; the db cannot be reasoned about safely. action: roll back the partial changes manually, then rerun the migration after fixing the concurrent index build issue.

logs.message: scheduling cron job at 02:00 (server tz=UTC)
next run computed to be in the past: 2026-05-06T01:30:00 (DST shift not handled)
cron triggered twice in the same hour due to DST fallback

gold: the cron schedule does not handle the dst fallback so the job ran twice in the same hour. action: schedule cron in utc and convert to local time only at the boundary, or use a scheduler that is dst-aware.

logs.message: computing avg latency p50 over 0 samples
division by zero in metric aggregation; emitting NaN
datadog rejected payload: 'NaN' is not a valid metric value

gold: the metric aggregator divided by zero samples and emitted NaN, which datadog rejected as invalid. action: gate the aggregation on n_samples > 0 and emit a default or skip the data point when there is nothing to aggregate.

logs.message: secrets manager: AWS/RDS/master rotated 02:14:33 UTC
FATAL: password authentication failed for user 'app'
service still using cached credential issued 04:00:00 UTC; not yet picked up rotation

gold: rds master credential was rotated but the service is still using the cached previous credential and getting authentication failures. action: invalidate the in-process credential cache on rotation; subscribe to secrets manager rotation events instead of caching forever.

logs.message: internal queue depth=9800/10000 (98% full)
dropping oldest events to keep up: dropped=120
downstream consumer cannot keep up; backpressure -> data loss

gold: the internal queue is full and the producer started dropping events; downstream is too slow. action: add real backpressure that pushes back to the producer instead of dropping; scale the consumer or lower the producer rate.

logs.message: outbound call api.partner.example pending dns lookup
dns resolution took 4200ms (resolver=169.254.169.253)
request timed out at the http client (5s budget) — most spent in dns

gold: dns resolution is taking 4+ seconds against the configured resolver and the http client's overall timeout is being eaten by it. action: switch to a faster resolver or local cache, and set a separate dns timeout shorter than the request timeout.

logs.message: spring application starting up
BeanCurrentlyInCreationException: Error creating bean with name 'orderService': Requested bean is currently in creation: Is there an unresolvable circular reference?
application context failed to start

gold: spring detected an unresolvable circular reference involving orderService during startup; the application context cannot finish booting. action: break the cycle by introducing an interface, an event listener, or @Lazy injection on one side.

logs.message: consumed kafka message offset=8421 size=1.2KB
json.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
raw payload starts with bytes: 0x1f 0x8b 0x08 (looks gzipped, expected json)
unable to decode message; producer may have changed serialization without coordination

gold: the consumer received a gzipped payload but its decoder expects raw json; this looks like an uncoordinated change on the producer side. action: align the producer/consumer on a single serialization format and version; reject and dlq malformed messages.

logs.message: goroutines=1024 heap_in_use=512MB
goroutines=18432 heap_in_use=2.1GB (still growing)
pprof shows 17000 goroutines blocked on channel receive in http.handleStream

gold: the service is leaking goroutines that block on a channel receive in http.handleStream; heap and goroutine count keep climbing under load. action: ensure every goroutine has a cancellation path (context with timeout or close on the receiving channel).

logs.message: ntp not synced; offset=+247s drift=growing
aws sigv4 signature rejected: RequestTimeTooSkewed (server time 247s ahead of aws)
all outbound s3 calls failing with 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch

gold: the host's clock is 247 seconds ahead of aws's clock so sigv4 signatures are rejected and all s3 calls fail with 403. action: fix ntp on the host and add a watchdog that alarms if drift exceeds 60s.

logs.message: alb health check on /healthz returning 200
/readyz returning 503 db_pool=exhausted but /healthz still 200
alb keeps routing traffic: health probe checks /healthz instead of /readyz

gold: the alb health check is hitting /healthz which always returns 200 even when the app is not actually able to serve requests; /readyz reports the truth and is not what the lb checks. action: point the lb health check at /readyz so unhealthy pods are pulled out.

logs.message: consumer p0 lag=2 p1 lag=8 p2 lag=14000 p3 lag=4
p2 producer using key='checkout' for 92% of messages — single key bucket
downstream p99 latency rising due to partition hotspot

gold: one partition is hot because 92% of producer messages use the same key, and the assigned consumer cannot keep up. action: change the partition key to a higher-cardinality field, or salt it, so load spreads evenly across partitions.

logs.message: received SIGTERM from k8s; pod terminating
in-flight requests count=42; no shutdown handler registered
process killed by SIGKILL after 30s grace; 42 client requests dropped

gold: the pod received SIGTERM but no shutdown handler is registered, so 42 in-flight requests were dropped when SIGKILL fired after the grace period. action: register a signal handler that stops accepting new connections and drains in-flight requests within the grace window.

logs.message: POST /webhook payload received from partner=acme
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'amount'
webhook handler crashed: optional field 'transaction.amount' was null but assumed present

gold: the webhook handler assumed transaction.amount is always present but the partner sent a payload where it is null. action: validate the incoming payload at the boundary (pydantic, json schema) and either reject or default the field before downstream code reads it.

logs.message: consuming from orders.v2 topic schema=2026-01-04
unexpected field 'tax_breakdown' in payload (not in our local schema 2026-01-04)
ProtoDecodeError: producer schema 2026-04-30 added required field; consumer not updated

gold: the producer started emitting a new required field but the consumer's locally pinned schema is out of date, so the protobuf decode fails. action: align the schema registry with the consumer and ensure consumers are updated before producers emit incompatible changes.

logs.message: upstream payments returned 503; retrying immediately (no backoff)
5x retries in 1s from 200 in-flight requests = 1000 rps to payments
payments service circuit broken: retry storm caused by missing exponential backoff

gold: 5x retries with no backoff against the payments service amplified normal load to 1000rps and tripped the circuit. action: add exponential backoff with full jitter, cap retries, and gate retries behind a circuit breaker.

logs.message: rds idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=300s; client pool max_idle=600s
psycopg2.OperationalError: server closed the connection unexpectedly
every checkout from pool fails first attempt; client max_idle exceeds server timeout

gold: the client's idle connection lifetime exceeds the rds idle_in_transaction_session_timeout, so checked-out connections are dead-on-arrival. action: set the client max_idle below the server side timeout (e.g. 240s vs server's 300s).

logs.message: tomcat thread pool max=200; current active=200
150 of 200 workers blocked on http client read from upstream-x (no read timeout set)
service unable to accept new connections; one slow upstream blocked the entire worker pool

gold: the http client to upstream-x has no read timeout so 150 of 200 worker threads are blocked waiting; the service can no longer accept new connections. action: set a read timeout on the http client and bound the pool to fail fast.

logs.message: request handler logging at DEBUG: 8000 lines/req
stdout pipe is blocking; cpu 78% in write() syscalls
request latency p99=12s; root cause: app blocked writing to a slow log sink

gold: debug logging is producing 8000 lines per request and stdout writes are blocking the request thread, pushing p99 to 12s. action: drop log level for the hot path, ship logs through an async sink, or non-blocking pipe.

logs.message: txn-X started: long-running ETL UPDATE on orders
300 unrelated SELECTs queued waiting for row lock held by txn-X
checkout p99=42s caused by long-running update transaction holding locks

gold: an etl update transaction is holding row locks on the orders table for an extended period, blocking 300 unrelated checkouts. action: shorten the etl transaction (chunked updates), use a replica for read-heavy etl, or schedule it during low traffic.

logs.message: POST /validate received user input length=8192
regex /^(a+)+$/ matching against 'aaaa...!' for 4200ms
request timed out at proxy after 5s; cpu pinned at 100% on regex backtracking

gold: the regex /^(a+)+$/ is exhibiting catastrophic backtracking on adversarial input and pinning cpu for 4+ seconds. action: rewrite the regex to be linear or switch to a regex engine without backtracking; cap input length at the boundary.

logs.message: scheduling reminder for user_local_time=09:00 IST
stored as 09:00 in db; db tz=UTC, app assumed IST
reminder fired 5h30m early for 12k users due to timezone mismatch between app and db

gold: the application stored a local time without timezone info in a utc-typed db column so reminders fired 5h30m early for ist users. action: always store timestamptz, convert to utc at the boundary, and present in user-local time only at render.

logs.message: k8s readiness probe passed at t=2s after start
jit warmup not complete; first 30s p99=8s vs steady state p99=200ms
rolling deploy: every new pod served 30s of slow traffic before warm; cumulative spike

gold: the readiness probe goes green at t=2s but the jvm jit isn't warm until ~30s, so each rolling-deploy pod served slow traffic for half a minute. action: add a warmup hook (synthetic requests) before /readyz turns green; or use a slower probe initial-delay.

logs.message: node-A acquired leader lease for nightly-billing
node-B acquired leader lease for nightly-billing (lease ttl race)
billing job ran twice for the same period; duplicate invoice rows in stripe

gold: two nodes acquired the leader lease for nightly-billing because of a ttl race in the election protocol; the job ran twice. action: use fencing tokens or a single-writer guarantee (e.g. transactional outbox) so duplicate execution can't produce duplicate side effects.

logs.message: calling partner /v1/charge with field 'amount_cents'
partner response: 400 unknown_field amount_cents (expected 'amount_minor_units')
all charges failing; partner deployed breaking field rename without versioning

gold: the partner renamed amount_cents to amount_minor_units without a versioned endpoint, so every charge now fails with 400. action: pin to a versioned partner endpoint; fall back to a feature-flagged code path that uses the new field name.

logs.message: outbound https://api.partner.example via corp proxy 10.0.0.5:3128
proxy 403 Forbidden: destination not in allowlist (request_id=cp-9821)
all partner.example calls blocked; security team's egress allowlist out of date

gold: the corporate egress proxy is blocking https://api.partner.example because it is not in the allowlist, so all partner calls return 403. action: get the destination added to the egress allowlist and add a synthetic check that watches for proxy 403s.

logs.message: outbound to checkout.svc.cluster.local
envoy x-cluster=checkout-staging instead of checkout-prod
production traffic routed to staging cluster; recent virtualservice change introduced a bad selector

gold: an envoy virtualservice rule selector now matches production traffic and routes it to the staging cluster. action: revert the virtualservice change and add an integration check that pins prod -> prod cluster.

logs.message: kafka group orders-consumer state=PreparingRebalance generation=42
rebalance taking >30s; one member is unresponsive (member_id=k-7e00e78d)
consumer group stuck in PreparingRebalance for 90s; lag growing 8000/s

gold: the kafka consumer group is stuck in PreparingRebalance because one member is unresponsive; lag is growing fast. action: kick the unresponsive member (force exit), tighten session.timeout.ms, and investigate the slow member.

logs.message: g1 gc full=12 mixed=300 young=4500 in last hour
old gen humongous regions=24% (threshold 40%); fragmentation rising
to-space exhausted during young gc; full gc pause 8s caused by humongous allocation

gold: g1gc is running into to-space exhaustion during young gc because humongous regions have fragmented the old generation. action: tune G1HeapRegionSize larger or refactor the allocation pattern that produces humongous objects (large strings/arrays).

logs.message: incoming GET /me with 18 cookies size=42KB
nginx returned 431 Request Header Fields Too Large
users with stale auth cookies + tracking cookies + experiment cookies hit the 32KB limit

gold: the user's accumulated cookies exceed nginx's request header limit and the proxy is returning 431 before the request reaches the app. action: prune unused cookies, raise large_client_header_buffers, or move tracking state out of cookies entirely.

logs.message: starting outbound calls; resolv.conf nameserver=10.0.0.99
resolver 10.0.0.99 not responding to queries (timeouts)
all outbound https calls failing with NameResolutionError; resolver IP is wrong after recent vpc change

gold: the configured nameserver in resolv.conf is unreachable after the recent vpc change, so all outbound dns is failing. action: fix /etc/resolv.conf or the dhcp option set; add a synthetic dns check.

logs.message: INSERT into events; sequence events_id_seq nextval contention
events_id_seq advisory lock held p99=80ms; insert throughput plateaued at 8000/s
single hot sequence is the bottleneck during peak; consider sharding or uuid v7

gold: the events_id_seq sequence is the throughput bottleneck on inserts during peak. action: switch to ulid/uuid v7 for the primary key or shard the sequence, removing the single-point of contention.

logs.message: rolling deploy: 3/10 pods on new image v1.2.3, 7/10 on v1.2.2
v1.2.3 introduced new request field; v1.2.2 pods 400 on those requests
30% of traffic failing during deploy: incompatible request schema across pod versions

gold: during the rolling deploy, v1.2.3 introduced a request schema field that v1.2.2 pods reject as 400; for the duration of the rollout, ~30% of traffic fails. action: make schema changes additive and backwards-compatible, or use a request-shape feature flag with a deploy-then-enable sequence.
